metadata.revenue_label: AirDNA Revenue Potential, last 12 months: modeled revenue, not actual income.
metadata.sample: 56 adult-themed listings in 40 cities (team keyword discovery), 54 with live public pages. Conventional comps were photo-reviewed per listing for comparable interiors and property style.

ladder.label: Hot tub + cabin-style or mountain/lake destination
Rung 2 + real kit (2+ pieces incl. cross or swing) + finish 3/5+
Rung 3 listings at $100K+ (7 of 11 from repeat operators)

steps: The gate. No listing without one reaches $100K, and those listings only match their own comps.
Hot-tub city houses, apartments and suites top out around $49K. A cabin, A-frame or treehouse in a mountain/lake destination moves the median up.
The first rung where $100K is likely. Hot-tub cabins with only a lit “secret room” all stay under $100K.
Within rung 3, the $100K+ listings run $391 ADR and 83% occupancy vs. $307 and 66%. Seven of the 11 come from operators running 2–3 adult listings.

rung_examples.0: Erotic Oasis, Baltimore ($7K); Siren’s Cozy Cove, Philadelphia ($36K)
rung_examples.1: Kinky Nights, Nashville apartment ($51K); Phoenix guest house ($35K)
rung_examples.2: Clayton “secret room” cabin ($86K); Sugar & Spice, Broken Bow ($73K); Sautee Nacoochee ($57K)
rung_examples.3: Velvet Chains ($132K) and Tangled Up ($117K), Blue Ridge; Dark Delight, Sevierville ($83K); Romantic Red Room, McCaysville ($91K)
rung_examples.Top: Red Room Cabins, Dunlap TN ($130–183K); Your Spicy Stay, Broken Bow & Sevierville ($107–111K); Banner Elk ski cabin ($132K)

traditional: Median $79K with one vs. $37K without. Listings with a hot tub beat their comps by +70%; those without are roughly level (−3%).
Mountain/lake destinations: $94K median vs. $46K in cities and $39K in small towns. 11 of the 13 listings above $100K are cabins, A-frames or a treehouse.
Basic or dated finishes: about $28K and no premium over comps. Updated finishes (3–4/5): +61–81%. Full luxury did not add more in this set.
Table stakes across the middle and top tiers (fire pit $78K vs. $51K).
In mountain markets, listings with and without a view earn about the same ($91K vs. $95K).
kink_points: Core kit: St. Andrew’s cross, swing, spanking bench, tantra chair, restraint points on the bed, red/LED lighting and a clean toy display. Every listing above $100K has a swing; 92% have a cross.
A credible kit is enough. Moving from a lighting-only “secret room” to a real, photographed setup is the step that matters; more pieces beyond that do not keep raising the premium.
Romance-only rooms (intensity 1/5) underperform comps by about 41% (3 with comps). Full dungeons earn high rates at lower occupancy, which makes them a niche product.
Skip the pole: it is more common in the lower tier and in city “bachelorette” party houses.
patterns: Among comparable themed hot-tub cabins, a dedicated playroom or a zone in the main bedroom: $107–112K median, vs. $79K when equipment is scattered across the house.
Exterior, view or hot-tub cover photos: $132K median vs. $79K for living-room covers (comparable themed cabins).
$117K vs. $101K among comparable themed cabins. 3–4 bedroom houses underperform (−16% vs. comps); most are city party houses.
A separate normal bedroom goes with higher revenue overall ($72K vs. $49K), but not once like-for-like cabins are compared. Treat it as a guest-experience standard.
The 6 listings coded oversized did not outperform. Photos cannot establish room size; testing it requires floor plans.
The operator matters at the top
Branded repeat operators turn about $100K into $130–180K through pricing power and occupancy.

answer.title: Yes, in the right cabin.
answer.title_em: The theme multiplies a strong getaway.
answer.deck: A themed hot-tub cabin in a mountain or lake getaway market earns about 50% more modeled revenue than comparable conventional cabins, and it is the only profile that regularly reaches $100K. City units earn far less ($37–49K medians), and themed listings without a hot tub only match their comps.

points: Required: a private hot tub. No listing without one reaches $100K.
A cabin, A-frame or treehouse in a mountain/lake destination ($94K median vs. $46K in cities).
Updated finishes (3/5 or better), a fire pit and outdoor dining.
Helpful, not required: views, a sauna, a spa bathroom.

questions.q: Which kink amenities and design patterns?
questions.a: A credible core kit, not a maximal dungeon.
points: Core kit: St. Andrew’s cross, swing, spanking bench, tantra chair, bed restraints, red/LED lighting.
Every listing above $100K has a swing; 92% have a cross.
No real equipment: −25% vs. comps. One to three pieces: already +71%.
Avoid lighting-only “secret rooms” and stripper poles.

questions.q: What else goes with stronger performance?
questions.a: Contained play space, the getaway photo and the operator.
points: Keep play in one dedicated room or the main bedroom ($107–112K vs. $79K when scattered).
Lead listing photos with the exterior, view or hot tub ($132K vs. $79K).
Two bedrooms edge out one ($117K vs. $101K); 3–4 bedroom party houses lag.
Branded repeat operators reach $130–183K. Oversized master bedrooms are not supported by the data.

buy: A 1–2 bedroom cabin or A-frame with a private hot tub in a proven mountain/lake getaway market.
Room for one dedicated play space alongside a normal sleeping bedroom.
The core kit, decent finishes and a cover photo that sells the setting first.
An operator with premium pricing discipline: the top listings run about $390+ ADR at 80%+ occupancy.
Underwrite against premium conventional cabins in the same market, never against a citywide average.
answer.confidence: Directional evidence. Both samples were discovered rather than randomly drawn, revenue is AirDNA’s modeled figure and comp sets are small. The gap is an observed association, not a guaranteed uplift.

caveats: A discovered set of 56 listings, not a random sample; higher rungs contain only 4–20 listings each.
Revenue Potential is modeled and flatters young listings (15 of 56 have fewer than 300 active nights).
Gaps are associations with a few reviewed comps, not causal theme effects or return estimates. 18 listings have no usable comp.
Photo coding reflects public galleries on October 27, 2026; not shown does not mean absent.
The 56-listing set uses a newer AirDNA pull than the 15 confirmed-cabin comparisons; the two are reported separately.
